content:
Hi everyone! I'm Thiago, born in Brazil and currently based in Montreal.

  • I'm interested in how formal methods can complement empirical ML work, especially when it comes to specifying and verifying safety-critical behaviours in LLMs and autonomous systems.
  • I'm the Community Manager at BAIF, where I'm working to build what I think could be the most intentional, thoughtful, and fun community in the AI safety space — one that doesn't quite exist yet, but should. DM me if you have thoughts on how to get there.
  • I've lived in a lot of places: New Delhi, Lisbon, Caracas, Brasilia, Boston, Ottawa, and now Montreal which finally feels like home.
  • Outside of work, I'm a sports junkie: soccer, runs along the canal, OrangeTheory, and badminton.

This is the place to introduce yourself: who you are, what you work on, and what brought you here.

There's no template, but if you want one:

  • Name and where you're based
  • What you work on (research, engineering, policy, other)
  • Your connection to formal verification or AI safety deep expert, curious newcomer, or anywhere in between
  • One thing you're hoping to get from this community
  • Something non-work we're people first

Don't overthink it. A few lines is fine. We'll start scroll up to read my intro and feel free to go from there.

Hi All! I'm Filippo, from Italy, currently based in Saint-Étienne, France.

  • I'm an associate professor in Math, working in formalised mathematics. I'm particularly interested in formalising Number Theory and Functional Analysis and alongside my research work I'm a strong advocate for Open Science and am part of several political bodies related to this matter. I'm being collaborating with BAIF since December under @Oliver Butterley and @Shaowei Lin .
  • I'm a Mathlib maintainer and was part of the LTE team, so my connection is through Lean/Mathlib.
  • I hope to get a perspective of the use of Lean and of the formalisation of Number Theory outside the purely academic world. I hope to understand metaprogramming in Lean much better than I do now, hopefully getting my hands dirty with Aeneas.
  • I've also lived in several places (Heidelberg, Berlin, Osaka, Exeter, Rome, Leiden, Caen, Vancouver...) and I love sailing, trying to get on a sailing boat as soon as I can. Failing that, I like studying Hebrew (modern, ancient, or in between), classical music, and playing padel.

I am Shreyas. Currently based in Saarbrucken, Germany.

  • I am currently a PhD student, soon to be a postdoc, who works at the intersection of CS theory and Lean. During my PhD I have designed and tested asynchronous ASICs, worked on clock synchronisation theory, and worked on lean in several ways.
  • I am definitely not a beginner in lean at this point. I hesitate to attach expertise tags. I was a contributor and maintainer at the equational theories project, to mention a prominent example. I am currently working on Algolean as a library for theoretical CS researchers. Early days.
  • I want to learn what verifying a real cryptographic protocol entails, perhaps by getting some hands on experience, but mostly by reading these threads and understanding the design considerations. I am a cautious end-user of AI. I did write my masters thesis on machine teaching, but that was aeons ago and very theoretical.
  • I am learning to play the violin. I enjoy long distance biking tours. I dance Tango and a bit of Bachata. I can get by in 5 languages (so far). I read a lot, more recently (academic) history books. I have lived in Chennai, Pune, Oxford, and now Saarbrucken and visited many other cities. my musical tastes change all the time and are wide. Spotify says I heard 437 genres last year. I am not sure that's true. But it is pointing in the right direction.

Hi. I'm Orpheus. I'm founder of HΩ (https://horizonomega.org/) a non-profit focused on AI safety projects, such as the Guaranteed Safe AI Seminars. I'm based in Montréal. I'm a Lean beginner. I've been donating to Signal Foundation for years. Looking forward to keep track of Signal Shot, and contributing if I find the time.

Hello everyone! I'm Juan, from Spain and based in Valencia.

  • I'm a formal verification engineer at Runtime Verification and come from a formal backround in logic. While working at RV I've done plenty of security audits and formal verification engagements at the industry level, including recent Lean engagements for the Etherum Foundation.
  • I've been practising on formal verification for years. At the end of my masters became acquainted with Rocq to verify some Proof Theory results and kept researching industrial applications. Shifted to work on the K framework at RV, and for more than a year now I've been enjoying working with Lean!
  • Recently we were tasked with assessing formal verification with Aeneas. After this experience, I'm extremely thrilled with what can we achieve with it! If possible, I'm looking forward to collaborate with the Signal Shot project! Definitely looking forward to all the learnings that will stem from here.
  • Perhaps related to this project, I usually am the "let's switch to Signal" friend that will care about your digital rights :) I am pretty much into the privacy/tech conscious movements, and lately have been pulled to read on the effects of technology on culture. Besides the tech stuff, in my free time I like to hike, play piano and read as much as I can (among other things). If any of you want to chat about these topics, feel free to shoot me a message!

Hi! I am Riccardo, from Italy but based in Paris.

  • I am an associate professor at a math department and a mathlib maintainer, so may daily job is to fight against lean to prove theorems (especially in number theory).
  • I am mostly interested in mathematics and how to make formal verification easier for humans, and I especially like when formalization teaches us something in mathematics. For example I was involved in the Liquid Tensor Experiment where this happened and it was a pleasure.
  • I am not involved in software verification, but I am curious to see how it works, and I like cryptography, especially the mathematical aspects.
  • Outside Lean I am an amateur table tenni player, so I really like the ping emoji :ping_pong:

• Hi! I'm Markus, based in NYC but originally from Canada.
  • I am a PhD student at NYU
  • I work mostly on program logics for probabilistic programming languages. I am one of the developers of Iris-Lean, a framework for verifying programs using concurrent separation logic.
  • Mostly just observing, this is an ambitious project and I'm interested to see where it goes! I'm very interested in understanding how the Sym framework works for proving theorems at a large scale, and I'm curious to hear more about the Aeneas Rust model being applied especially in a security context. And of course, I'm interested to see if there's any opportunity for cross-pollination with Iris-Lean :)
  • Outside of Lean I love to dodge cars on my rollerblades

Hello everyone! I'm Matej based out of Chicago! I'm at BAIF working closely with Son Ho on Aeneas. I did my PhD at UIUC in geometric representation theory, but I've been doing Lean stuff since ~2022. I've mostly worked with Lean in the cryptography domain, but the last couple years I've been working to model and reason about program semantics.

I think I'll generally be involved with signal shot indirectly through my contributions to Aeneas/Charon and the tooling surrounding it. But maybe I'll be able to help write some proofs as well!

Hi all!

  • I'm Andrii originally from Ukraine, based in Bobigny, Paris now, previously spend quite a bit of time in Kazakhstan.
  • I'm software engineer which love to play (for now) with Lean, and popularize it in Ukrainian communities of software developers.
  • Unfortunately I have no connection to formal verification or AI safety, except my deep passion about the strictness of produced software.
  • I'm actually looking what I can bring to community, so I can get fun journey towards somewhere.
  • Outside of work, I actually like to have fun writing compilers, obfuscators, deobfuscators, promote better management practices for software developers in local community. Also love teachign programming and math to kids.

Hi all! I'm Sam Schlesinger. I'm based out of Connecticut in the USA. I work on Google Chrome on cryptography, security, and privacy and I am the co-chair of the Anti-Fraud Community Group in the W3C. I spend a lot of my free time lately proving things in Lean, mainly around cryptography, deep learning, and distributed systems but other random math and cs things too. I recently started a YouTube channel where I share my love for theoretical computer science, happy to share that if folks reach out but I don't want to advertise it here.

Outside of my intellectual interests, I enjoy watching the birds in my bird feeder, taking walks and hikes with my dog Nori, lifting weights, and street biking.

Hi everyone! I'm Nadim Kobeissi, based out of Paris, France. I work at Symbolic Software, where I've recently published research uncovering many weaknesses, false claims and vulnerabilities in both Cryspen's cryptographic libraries and formal verification stack (currently under peer review):

  • Verification Theatre: False Assurance in Formally Verified Cryptographic Libraries
  • Verification Facade: Masquerading Insecure Cryptographic Implementations as Verified Code

I received my PhD in applied cryptography and formal methods at Inria Paris in 2019. I recently finished teaching an applied cryptography course that I designed in Beirut, Lebanon, and am currently organizing Cedarcrypt, Lebanon's first applied cryptography conference being held this year in Paphos, Cyprus due to the current war. We have a great program and registration just opened last week, so check it out!

Hi! My name is Wrenna Robson - currently working as a research associate at the University of Bristol and based in Wales in the UK. I recently completed my PhD at Royal Holloway's Centre for Doctoral Training in Cybersecurity in the Everyday, submitting my thesis "Finding meaning in cryptographic verification" (https://pure.royalholloway.ac.uk/en/publications/finding-meaning-in-cryptographic-verification-methods-in-the-veri/). I am very interested in what "successful verification" actually means and extremely supportive of efforts to actually plan and produce a truly end to end chain of claims (I am very suspicious of research that on some level points to a succesful output from a verification tool and says 'that's done!' - that is the opposite of meaning, to me).

In other work I recently had accepted a paper to TCHES, "Veriﬁed non-recursive calculation of Beneš networks applied to Classic McEliece", where I worked with a PhD student at Bristol to turn a result that unexpectedly came out of some Lean work I did during my thesis, and turn it into a real implementation of a revised method for Beneš networks calculation that had real-wrold speedups (the speed-ups, I have to say, mostly came from Sam being a wizard with actually doing vectorised implementations, but they would not have been possible without the insight from the formalisation!)

I am very interested in what “successful verification” actually means

Preach, sister!

Hi everyone,

I'm Lalith, a PhD student in the University of Colorado's Programming Languages Lab. My background is in applied cryptography, with experience in blockchain and multiparty computation.

Last few months, I worked in Lean on the Needham-Schroeder protocol, proving that the original version is insecure under the Dolev-Yao attacker model and that the NSL extension is secure as a learning project.

Excited to be here and looking forward to learning from and contributing to the community.

Hi people! I'm Shaowei Lin, Chief Scientist at the Beneficial AI Foundation. I'm based in the San Francisco bay area. My research interests are in deductive program synthesis and the information theory of spiking neural networks.

My PhD was originally in Math, working on singular learning theory. Over the years, I've been exploring the entire theory-to-application spectrum, working in a university, in a govt-research organization, in mission-driven non-profits, and in a tech start-up. I've been thinking about what it means to grow research ideas into artifacts that can impact societies. I've been obsessing over the use of formal methods (type theory and category theory) to constrain and guide the actions of reinforcement learners.

To me, Signal Shot is not just about verifying Signal. It is more about building tools (including formal, collaborative and AI tools) that can change the way safe software development is done. I hope to learn from all of you in these aspects. In my free time, I love to run/hike/swim/bike - anything that can let my mind wander for a long period of time.

Hi! I'm Sebastian Verschoor, a postdoc researcher at UvA/QuSoft (in Amsterdam).

  • I've been working on pen-and-paper proofs for cryptographic protocols (mostly AKE), and I am seeing an increased need to formally verify these proofs.
  • At the same time I see that people are formalizing quantum information in Lean, and I hope to apply their results to cryptography, so that we can formally verify post-quantum security. Doing this for Signal right now feels like an unrealistic first target, but who knows how fast things can go when supported by AI tooling...
  • Outside of work I like rock climbing and playing classical guitar.

Hi I am Sparsa,
I am a Verification Engineer. I completed my PhD in Theory of Computation with specialisation in formal methods. I am incorporating Lean as an executable and provable specification in my work.
I am super interested in project and I am looking forward to contribute to it.

Hey everyone, I'm David. I have some relevant industry experience in Rust, applied cryptography, and software engineering (can read here if interested: https://davidnugent.net). I also enjoyed a formal verification course I did on Dafny back when I was in university. I recently started a small R&D lab, Breaks & Ciphers, focused on open-source cybersecurity, cryptography, and privacy.
Signal Shot seems like it could be a great initiative to contribute to. I just watched the video of the talks you gave recently, and I'm eager to see which community contributions you're looking for first!

Hello! I'm a master's student at the University of Washington and work at the Freedom of the Press Foundation on the SecureDrop Protocol for whistleblower communications, which we've modeled in Tamarin (in collaboration with ETH Zurich, under peer review) and for which we're exploring implementation verification. We'll be following this effort closely to see what we can learn from Lean-based approaches.

Hello! I am Vighnesh, currently based in Mumbai/Chennai, India.
I am a undergrad student, majoring in CS. Currently I am just exploring computer science, for the past year I have worked with Rust and a tiny amount of verilog.
I am just a newcomer interested in learning to use lean to formally verify software.
I would love to learn a lot about lean, formal verification and contribute in the process.
Outside of work, I love to play badminton and tinker with radios.

Hi everyone, I'm Jie from Natuvea, where we build an end-to-end encrypted
messaging platform on top of libsignal. Signal Shot drew me in because I care a lot about libsignal being correct in the actual code, not just on paper, which is exactly what this project is about.
My background is Rust plus a strong testing and assurance discipline. Our team recently filed a couple of upstream libsignal issues on the FFI/build and dependency side, so we know the codebase a little. I'm newer to Lean and Aeneas but keen to learn them here, and I'm eager to see where a Rust and crypto person could help first.

Hello! I am John and I am a recent mathematics graduate from VU Amsterdam. I have made a few contributions to mathlib previously with help from Christian Mertens, so I am somewhat knowledgeable about Lean and project collaboration. I am hoping to further improve my formalisation skills and learn a little more about cryptography. In my spare time, I like to read books and play cheap steam games.

Hey folks! I'm Anders, a Professional Master's student in CS at University of Washington and a C++ graphics/systems engineer. I've been leaning into verification and PLs in coursework and I hope to get my hands dirty with some real-world contributions here. Outside of work I can be found rock climbing, skateboarding and roller skating around Seattle
